tytul: Swedish stirred lingonberries (rårörda lingon) for the refrigerator or freezer
wstep: This card follows the Marthaförbundet recipe for lingonberries crushed with sugar without cooking; JarAtlas keeps them within the NCHFP limits for uncooked jams: up to 3 weeks in the refrigerator or up to a year in a freezer.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Uncooked fruit with sugar molds or ferments in a short time at room temperature, according to NCHFP, so keep the lingonberries only in the refrigerator or freezer.

akapity: A 2023 study of wild lingonberries measured a pH of 2.66–3.03.
According to Marthaförbundet, lingonberries contain benzoic acid, which gives stirred lingonberries a long life in the refrigerator; the source gives no number of days.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): because the source gives no number of days, JarAtlas uses the NCHFP limits for uncooked jams.
1 litre of lingonberries and 1 dl of sugar.
Sterilize canning jars and prepare two-piece canning lids according to the manufacturer’s directions.
Sort and wash fully ripe berries, drain them and remove any stems, as NCHFP directs for uncooked berry jam.
Crush the berries with the sugar using a masher or a stick blender; a mixer gives a runnier result.
Spoon them into the jars, close the jars and put them in the refrigerator or freezer straight away.
Store the lingonberries up to 3 weeks in the refrigerator or up to a year in a freezer.
Keep an opened container in the refrigerator and use the lingonberries within a few days.

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves.
